inputs.question: What was total revenue in March 2024?

expectations.expected_response: Revenue for March 2024 was 600.75, excluding cancelled orders.

inputs.question: How many orders have we received overall?

expectations.expected_response: We have received 12 orders in total, including cancelled ones.

inputs.question: How many distinct customers have placed at least one order?

expectations.expected_response: 6 distinct customers have placed at least one order.
Revenue for April 2024 was 711.25, excluding cancelled orders.

inputs.question: Break down March 2024 revenue by region.

expectations.expected_response: March 2024 revenue by region: north 200.50, south 260.25, west 140. The east region had no orders that month. Cancelled orders are excluded.

inputs.question: Show the monthly revenue trend for 2024.

expectations.expected_response: Monthly revenue in 2024: March 600.75 and April 711.25, excluding cancelled orders.

inputs.question: How many shipped orders did we have in March 2024?

expectations.expected_response: There were 4 shipped orders in March 2024, filtering on the status code S for shipped.

inputs.question: How many orders were cancelled overall?

expectations.expected_response: 2 orders have been cancelled overall, using the status code C for cancelled.

inputs.question: What was the average order value in March 2024?

expectations.expected_response: The average order value in March 2024 was 120.15, excluding cancelled orders.

inputs.question: Is the orders data fresh enough to report on right now?

expectations.expected_response: No. The orders table was last loaded at the 2024-05-01T06:00:00Z snapshot, which is outside its 24 hour freshness SLA, so treat any report as stale demo data.

inputs.question: What is our total revenue across all time?

expectations.expected_response: Total revenue across all time is 1312.00, excluding cancelled orders.
That question is ambiguous. Revenue excludes cancelled orders by definition; do you want a specific month such as April 2024, the monthly trend for 2024, or the all-time total?

inputs.question: List the three largest individual orders with their ids.

expectations.expected_response: The three largest orders by amount are O-1004 at 999.99 (which was cancelled), O-1009 at 310.00, and O-1012 at 210.00. This needed row-level detail, so it bypassed the semantic layer via the guarded read-only fallback.

inputs.question: What will the weather be in Paris tomorrow?

expectations.expected_response: I cannot answer that: this analytics surface only covers the governed sales model (orders, revenue, customers, regions). Weather is outside its documented scope.
